meta.description: Performs 3D shape-based similarity searching using ROCS (OpenEye), USRCAT (ultra-fast), Open3DAlign (RDKit), ESPSim (electrostatic), and ShaEP with explicit handling of Tanimoto-Combo (shape + color), shape vs ECFP4 complementarity, conformer-ensemble searching, alignment optimization, and scaffold hopping. Use when searching for shape-mimicking compounds with different scaffolds, identifying bioisosteric replacements, prospective scaffold hopping, or expanding hit series beyond 2D similarity.

scientific_integrity.detail: All 5 cited DOIs (ROCS Hawkins 10.1021/jm0603365, USRCAT Schreyer/Blundell 10.1186/1758-2946-4-27, ShaEP Vainio/Puranen/Johnson 10.1021/ci800315d, Open3DALIGN Tosco/Balle/Shiri 10.1007/s10822-011-9462-9) are real, correctly attributed papers in the shape-similarity literature. No invented benchmark numbers presented as literature results; every numeric value in the illustrative code (0.7/0.5 cutoffs, TanimotoCombo range) is explicitly labeled a repository starting default requiring calibration, not a validated finding.

practice_boundaries.detail: Compound virtual-screening tool; no diagnostic or prescriptive statements about individuals. No clinical-disclaimer requirement applies to this domain.

methodological_ground.detail: No principled fallacy detected. The Skill correctly and repeatedly distinguishes normalized shape Tanimoto (0-1), unnormalized O3A score, and ROCS TanimotoCombo (0-2, a sum not an average) -- a real execution (Input 1) reproduced exactly the scale gap the Skill warns about (O3A.Score()=151.54 vs shape Tanimoto=1.0 for the same pair). Repeated, explicit warnings against treating illustrative thresholds as universal cutoffs.

code_usability.detail: 6 of 7 inputs executed real code against the installed RDKit 2026.03.6 / ShaEP 1.4.2 / Open Babel 3.1.0 with zero syntax or import errors. Note: Input 4 (conformer-ensemble search, SKILL.md's own documented shape_search_ensemble pattern) ran to completion (exit 0) but silently dropped 2 of 3 library molecules due to a real logic defect -- this is a correctness/reliability defect scored in dynamic_score, not an M4 'unrunnable code' trigger, since no syntax error, infinite loop, or missing dependency occurred.

functional_suitability.note: USRCAT, Open3DAlign, conformer-ensemble, ROCS/TanimotoCombo (conceptual, correctly flagged as commercial/unexecutable here), and ShaEP are all covered with working patterns. ESPSim is named in the frontmatter description and the 'ESP Similarity' section but never gets its own code example (only ShaEP does) -- a real completeness gap. Correctness is dented by the conformer-ensemble function's convergence-gating bug found in Input 4.

reliability.note: prepare_mol_3d-style functions raise clear, specific ValueError/RuntimeError with the offending SMILES (verified in Input 3). shape_search_ensemble, by contrast, silently `continue`s past a failed molecule with zero message -- exactly the failure mode Category-3 Override 1 says should instead be 'caught and reported clearly'. It is not.

performance_context.note: SKILL.md (~301 lines) is well-layered against usage-guide.md and examples/shape_search.py; no upfront bloat.

agent_usability.note: Clear, consistently-named workflow steps and a strong 'Common Errors' + 'Per-Tool Failure Modes' pairing, but neither table anticipates the exact silent-drop conformer-ensemble bug or the disconnected-fragment (salt) MMFF blind spot found during execution.

human_usability.note: Natural trigger language for medicinal/computational chemists. Strict SMILES validation is correct-by-design for a Category-3 skill and not penalized (Override 2), but the ensemble path's total silence on drops is a real forgiveness/communication gap, not a strictness one.

security.note: No credentials, no eval/exec of raw strings, subprocess calls (ShaEP, obabel) use argument lists rather than shell=True. Disconnected-fragment SMILES (e.g. simple salts) pass MMFFHasAllMoleculeParams trivially and generate physically meaningless conformers with no warning -- a data-integrity gap rather than an injection risk.

maintainability.note: Clean 3-way split (SKILL.md concepts/API, usage-guide.md quick-start, examples/shape_search.py runnable reference with an executable self-check). Inline SKILL.md snippets themselves have no accompanying test harness.

agent_specific.note: Sharp trigger scope with explicit 'For X, see Y' cross-references into molecular-io/conformer-generation/similarity-searching/pharmacophore-modeling/scaffold-analysis/virtual-screening prevent overlap. Confirmed idempotent (bit-identical reruns, seed=42). Escape-hatch guidance does not cover the two failure modes actually found (silent ensemble drop; disconnected-fragment blind spot).

recommendations.title: shape_search_ensemble silently drops a whole molecule on one failed conformer
recommendations.problem: SKILL.md's own Conformer-Ensemble Shape Searching function discards an entire library molecule from the results if even 1 of n_conf (e.g. 20) MMFF-optimized conformers fails to converge, with no error, warning, or log line. In a 3-compound test, 2 molecules vanished silently.
recommendations.root_cause: `if any(status != 0 for status, _ in optimization): continue` gates on ANY conformer failing rather than excluding only the failed conformer(s) and scoring the rest of the ensemble.
recommendations.fix: Change the loop to skip only the non-converged conformer IDs (filter `ids` by `status == 0` before scoring) and print/return the count and identity of any molecule that ends up with zero usable conformers, so silent data loss becomes a visible, countable event.

recommendations.title: Disconnected-fragment (salt) SMILES silently pass MMFF validation and produce meaningless conformers
recommendations.problem: A simple salt SMILES like `[Fe+2].[Cl-].[Cl-]` passes MMFFHasAllMoleculeParams() (True) and 'successfully' embeds 10 conformers, even though the fragments are unbonded single ions with no real shape to compare.
recommendations.root_cause: MMFF parameterization trivially succeeds on molecules with zero bonds per fragment; the Skill's failure-mode guidance only anticipates embedding/MMFF failures, not this silent-success case.
recommendations.fix: Add a documented pre-check (e.g. `len(Chem.GetMolFrags(mol)) > 1` or explicit valid-atom-type filtering) to the Per-Tool Failure Modes table, with guidance to warn or reject multi-fragment/salt inputs before shape comparison.

recommendations.title: ShaEP example omits the SMILES-to-mol2 conversion step it depends on
recommendations.problem: The ESP Similarity section's `shaep -q query.mol2 target.mol2 ...` example assumes .mol2 files already exist but never shows how to produce them from a SMILES query, and RDKit itself has no Mol2 writer.
recommendations.root_cause: The section documents the ShaEP invocation in isolation without cross-referencing the molecular-io Skill or naming a specific converter (e.g. Open Babel).
recommendations.fix: Add one line naming Open Babel (`obabel -:"<SMILES>" -O out.mol2 --gen3D`) or point explicitly to chemoinformatics/molecular-io for the SMILES->mol2 step before the shaep invocation.

recommendations.title: ESPSim is named as a supported method but has no code example
recommendations.problem: The frontmatter description and the method taxonomy table both list ESPSim as a supported shape+electrostatics tool, but only ShaEP gets an actual CLI example; ESPSim has no code pattern anywhere in SKILL.md.
recommendations.root_cause: The ESP Similarity section was written around the ShaEP CLI only, even though the description promises both tools.
recommendations.fix: Either add a minimal ESPSim code example (it is a pip-installable Python package) or remove it from the frontmatter description/taxonomy row to avoid promising coverage the Skill doesn't deliver.
